Estimates hold with every fixed number of log-coordinate derivatives when the source has the corresponding regularity, with an arbitrarily small loss in a stated polynomial power.*\n\n\n*Here the second-order differential perturbation $Q=\\mathcal L-\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ retains the strict principal accretivity of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>, with $E\\asymp e^{-2t}$, and, for the chosen $0<\\eta<1$, has the following gain on every fixed weight used in the assertion: $$\\label{lin:normalized-decay}\n \\|Qv\\|_{Y_{e^{(\\beta-2+\\eta)t},h}}\n       \\le C_{\\beta,h,\\eta}\\|v\\|_{X_{e^{\\beta t},h}}.$$ The analogous bound is required after the fixed translations and commutations used to obtain derivative estimates. Thus the changes of the radial, mixed, and angular principal coefficients are measured in their respective units $E$, $\\sqrt E$, and $1$; lower coefficient terms may instead be measured in the corresponding coefficient–module operator norm. Ordinary absolute decay of the radial coefficient is not the condition in <a href=\"#lin:normalized-decay\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:normalized-decay\">[lin:normalized-decay]</a>.*\n\n\n*Consequently, on each cylindrical end and for every small $\\eta>0$, $$\\label{lin:end-expansion}\n R-\\sqrt2=O(z^{-2+\\eta}),\\qquad\n J=c z^2+z(\\ell\\cdot e_r)+O(z^\\eta)$$ for a Gaussian Jacobi solution with compact source. If $c=0$, subtracting the exact infinitesimal rotation with tilt $\\ell$ leaves $O(z^{-2+\\eta})$. End solutions with arbitrary prescribed $c,\\ell$ exist, and their inward cutoffs have compact Jacobi source.",

        "anchor": "stmt-gauge-fiber-atlas",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\vartheta$ denote the finite end-rotation parameters. After fixing real coordinate identifications on the compact overlaps, the core and prescribed end graphs can be represented by one fiber map $$\\Gamma_\\vartheta(y,s),\\qquad \\Gamma_0(y,0)=X(y),$$ over the fixed real base atlas of $S$. It is smooth in $y$ and analytic in $(\\vartheta,s)$. It agrees with the fixed core graph map on the common observation support, independently of $\\vartheta$, and with the prescribed rotated radius or link map sufficiently far on each end. On the compact overlaps, $(y,s)\\mapsto\\Gamma_\\vartheta(y,s)$ is a local diffeomorphism for small real $(\\vartheta,s)$.         "anchor": "stmt-lin-family",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\kappa$ be the number of cylindrical ends. The observations can be chosen so that their values are $q=\\mathsf P(p)$ in analytic reduced coordinates $p=(b,x)\\in\\mathbb R^{m-\\kappa}\\times\\mathbb R^\\kappa$, with the following properties.*\n\n\n1.  *At $x=0$ there is a real analytic family $S_b$ of normalized solutions of <a href=\"#lin:normalized-equation\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:normalized-equation\">[lin:normalized-equation]</a>. It has the same end types as $S$, permits independent end tilts, and permits changes of its conical links within the normalized family. Outside the fixed observation support it is an exact shrinker. Its cylindrical remainder after rotating the end is $O(z^{-2+\\eta})$ for every fixed $\\eta>0$, on a parameter neighborhood that may depend on this choice. On each conical end its link graph satisfies $$\\label{lin:family-conical-asymptotics}\n     v_b(t,\\theta)=v_{b,\\infty}(\\theta)+O(e^{-2t})$$ in every fixed log and angular derivative, with $v_{b,\\infty}$ analytic in $b$. These bounds and their fixed parameter derivatives are uniform on a closed small parameter ball.*\n\n\n2.  *There is a unique formal normalized solution in $x$, $$u(b,x)\\sim\\sum_{\\alpha\\in\\mathbb N^\\kappa}u_\\alpha(b)x^\\alpha,\n     \\qquad\\lambda(b,x)\\sim\\sum_\\alpha\\lambda_\\alpha(b)x^\\alpha,$$ based at $S_b$, whose coefficients in the prescribed graph charts have polynomial growth and are analytic in $b$. For real $b$, their coefficientwise conversions to normal graph jets are smooth in $b$ and have uniform polynomial bounds at every fixed derivative order. After removal of the first-order tilt, the term homogeneous of degree one in $x$ on cylindrical end $j$ is $$\\label{lin:opening-coefficient}\n      \\frac{\\sqrt2}{2}\\,\\beta_j(b,x)z^2+O(|x|z^\\eta),\n      \\qquad \\beta(b,x)=M(b)x,$$ where $M(b)$ is an analytic invertible $\\kappa\\times\\kappa$ matrix. In particular $\\beta$ is exactly homogeneous linear in $x$ for fixed $b$.*\n\n\n3.  *Integrating the Gaussian action coefficient by coefficient defines $\\mathcal F\\in\\mathbb R\\{b\\}[[x]]$, with $$\\label{lin:action-multipliers}\n      \\nabla_p\\mathcal F=(D_p\\mathsf P)^{\\mathsf T}\\lambda.$$ Every fixed truncation of the prescribed graph series and every fixed number of its parameter or spatial derivatives has uniform polynomial end bounds on a sufficiently small complex $b$ neighborhood. The real normal truncations have the analogous smooth bounds for real parameters. This neighborhood may depend on the fixed truncation and derivative orders.*\n\n*When the limiting links and cylindrical directions are separated, as for the tangent section in [geo:tangent](#geo:tangent), the real family on a closed sufficiently small ball has the following additional geometry. Its smooth rescaled conical annuli, the rotated cylindrical tails, and the compact core have uniform bounded geometry. There is a uniform positive normal tubular radius; on a sufficiently far conical annulus of radius $r$ the tubular radius is at least $cr$. In the prescribed parametrizations $|\\partial_bX_b|\\le C(1+|X|)$ and its physical first derivative is bounded. These statements concern the real surfaces; complex parameter continuation is taken in the prescribed coordinates on a fixed real atlas.",

On each conical end its link graph satisfies $$\\label{lin:family-conical-asymptotics}\n     v_b(t,\\theta)=v_{b,\\infty}(\\theta)+O(e^{-2t})$$ in every fixed log and angular derivative, with $v_{b,\\infty}$ analytic in $b$. These bounds and their fixed parameter derivatives are uniform on a closed small parameter ball.*\n\n\n2.  *There is a unique formal normalized solution in $x$, $$u(b,x)\\sim\\sum_{\\alpha\\in\\mathbb N^\\kappa}u_\\alpha(b)x^\\alpha,\n     \\qquad\\lambda(b,x)\\sim\\sum_\\alpha\\lambda_\\alpha(b)x^\\alpha,$$ based at $S_b$, whose coefficients in the prescribed graph charts have polynomial growth and are analytic in $b$. For real $b$, their coefficientwise conversions to normal graph jets are smooth in $b$ and have uniform polynomial bounds at every fixed derivative order. After removal of the first-order tilt, the term homogeneous of degree one in $x$ on cylindrical end $j$ is $$\\label{lin:opening-coefficient}\n      \\frac{\\sqrt2}{2}\\,\\beta_j(b,x)z^2+O(|x|z^\\eta),\n      \\qquad \\beta(b,x)=M(b)x,$$ where $M(b)$ is an analytic invertible $\\kappa\\times\\kappa$ matrix. In particular $\\beta$ is exactly homogeneous linear in $x$ for fixed $b$.*\n\n\n3.  *Integrating the Gaussian action coefficient by coefficient defines $\\mathcal F\\in\\mathbb R\\{b\\}[[x]]$, with $$\\label{lin:action-multipliers}\n      \\nabla_p\\mathcal F=(D_p\\mathsf P)^{\\mathsf T}\\lambda.$$ Every fixed truncation of the prescribed graph series and every fixed number of its parameter or spatial derivatives has uniform polynomial end bounds on a sufficiently small complex $b$ neighborhood. The real normal truncations have the analogous smooth bounds for real parameters. This neighborhood may depend on the fixed truncation and derivative orders.*\n\n*When the limiting links and cylindrical directions are separated, as for the tangent section in [geo:tangent](#geo:tangent), the real family on a closed sufficiently small ball has the following additional geometry. Its smooth rescaled conical annuli, the rotated cylindrical tails, and the compact core have uniform bounded geometry. There is a uniform positive normal tubular radius; on a sufficiently far conical annulus of radius $r$ the tubular radius is at least $cr$. In the prescribed parametrizations $|\\partial_bX_b|\\le C(1+|X|)$ and its physical first derivative is bounded. These statements concern the real surfaces; complex parameter continuation is taken in the prescribed coordinates on a fixed real atlas.",

        "anchor": "stmt-ref-finite-taylor",
        "exact_quote": "For every fixed $M\\ge1$, let $v^{(M)}(b,x)$ be the coefficientwise real normal-height polynomial through degree $M$ in the opening variables, let $\\lambda_M$ be the multiplier polynomial, and let $f_M$ be the same truncation of $\\mathcal F$. On a smaller closed real $b$-neighborhood, each fixed spatial and real parameter derivative of the normal coefficients is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $1+|Y|$. The multiplier and action polynomials retain the analytic $b$ dependence of the prescribed-coordinate jets. For real parameters, $\\lambda_M-\\lambda_b=O(|x|)$.*\n\n*On every region where the absolute sum of the finite nonconstant height terms and their first two spatial derivatives is sufficiently small, the normalized equation of $v^{(M)}$ has an $L^2_a$ remainder at most $C_M|x|^{M+1}$. When the region contains the observation support, its observation error is at most $C_M|x|^{M+1}$. The corresponding local area integral differs by at most $C_M|x|^{M+1}$ from the integral of the normal-coordinate density coefficients determined by those finite normal jets through degree $M$ on that region. Their complete integrals sum to $f_M$ for real parameters, and these normal density coefficients have Gaussian tails bounded by $C_M(1+r)^{d_M}e^{-c_Mr^2}$ outside $|Y|\\le r$.*\n\n\n\n\n*There is also a globally small real normal graph $T_M$, with height $\\widetilde v_M$ obtained by cutting off $v^{(M)}$ at a radius $|x|^{-\\sigma_M}$, and with $T_M=S_b$ when $x=0$, for which $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|\\mathcal N_b(\\widetilde v_M,\\lambda_M)\\|_{L^2_a}\n       &\\le C_M|x|^{M+1},\\label{ref:taylor-equation}\\\\\n |P(T_M)-\\mathsf P(p)|+|F(T_M)-f_M(p)|\n       &\\le C_M|x|^{M+1},\\label{ref:taylor-action}\\\\\n |\\nabla_p f_M(p)-J(p)^{\\mathsf T}\\lambda_M(p)|\n       &\\le C_M|x|^M,\\qquad J=D_p\\mathsf P.\n       \\label{ref:taylor-multiplier}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Its normal height has $C^2$ norm $O(|x|^{1/2})$.         "anchor": "stmt-arr-contours",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the finite list of nonzero leading opening coefficients. For every sufficiently large fixed $D$, there are upper and lower families of contours on sectors of the $a$-cover containing, respectively, the argument intervals $[0,\\pi]$ and $[-\\pi,0]$, with excess angle $\\delta=\\eta D^{-1/2}$, where $\\eta>0$ is fixed sufficiently small. The contours start on the real axis, satisfy <a href=\"#arr:path-signs\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"arr:path-signs\">[arr:path-signs]</a> strictly, avoid $1+\\beta z^2=0$, and end at $\\operatorname{Re}z^2=D/|a|$. They obey $|a||z|^2\\le C_D$. Their normalized derivatives and the inverse diffusion margins are bounded by constants depending on $D$.*\n\n*The families can be chosen smooth in sector parameters. As geometric paths they admit shortening, deformation before an adverse pole to a common real contour with endpoint at three quarters of the leading squared pole height, and deformation beyond that pole to the height turns used in the jump calculation. The bounded scaled part of these homotopies can be kept in $|R_c|\\ge r_*$ for a fixed $r_*>0$. The homothetic turns with shrinking $|R_c|$ retain the displayed geometric signs, but their solutions will be constructed in the separate height norms of [sec:jump](#sec:jump). Boundary data are specified by the solve statements below, not by this geometric lemma. These assertions persist in sufficiently small polynomial-radius complex balls about any fixed high-order polynomial approximation to $\\widehat p$.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $B\\ge1$ and, on a bounded interval, prescribe smooth circular reference functions and transverse coefficients $$X(t,\\theta)=(B\\zeta(t,\\theta),R(t,\\theta)e_r(\\theta)),\\quad\n \\zeta=\\zeta_0+c_1u,\\qquad R=R_0+c_2u.\n \\label{gauge:immersion}$$ Assume that $R_0$, $\\zeta_0'$ and $c_2\\zeta_0'-c_1R_0'$ are bounded away from zero, that their required fixed derivatives are bounded, and that the circular reference has the strict ellipticity margins of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a> after division by its drift. Constants may depend on these fixed margins.         "anchor": "stmt-gauge-height",
        "exact_quote": "Prescribe the polar height chart $$X=(Zg(r,\\theta),r e_r(\\theta))$$ on real parameters along a fixed complex $r$ contour. Let $|Z|\\asymp B$, $t=-\\log r$, and assume a uniformly bounded circular reference $g_0$ satisfies $|(g_0)_t|\\asymp |r|^2$, with its fixed log derivatives of this size. Assume $|Br|\\ge Y_0$ and put $E=|Br|^{-2}$ on each strip. The reference conditions include the full real pullback and drift division. More precisely, if $t=t(\\xi)$ on the real outward parameter and $J=t_\\xi$, assume $J,J^{-1}$ and their required fixed derivatives are bounded. Let $\\mathcal F_t(g)$ denote the left side of the log-normalized equation <a href=\"#gauge:polar-normalized\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"gauge:polar-normalized\">[gauge:polar-normalized]</a> below, including its graph-dependent $H_1$ division. Write its circular linearization in the log coordinate as $$D\\mathcal F_t(g_0)v=(1+d_{\\mathrm{ref}})v_t-a_{\\mathrm{ref}}v_{tt}\n       -c_{\\mathrm{ref}}v_{\\theta\\theta}+q_{\\mathrm{ref}}v.$$ Its full pulled drift is $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}=1+d_{\\mathrm{ref}}\n             +a_{\\mathrm{ref}}J_\\xi/J^2$. Assume this is a bounded unit and that, after division by it, $$\\operatorname{Re}\\frac{a_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{J\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\ge cE,\n \\quad \\left|\\frac{a_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{J\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\right|\\le CE,\n \\quad \\operatorname{Re}\\frac{Jc_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\ge c,\n \\quad \\left|\\frac{Jc_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\right|\\le C.$$ The normalized coefficient derivatives and lower terms satisfy the bounds of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>. All metric and graph denominators in $\\mathcal F_t$ remain bounded analytic units in their normalized scales on the graph neighborhood. These are algebraic hypotheses on the prescribed reference, checked for the collapsing paths below. Let $\\operatorname{pb}_J$ mean the algebraic pullback obtained by replacing $\\partial_t$ with $J^{-1}\\partial_\\xi$ and reading all prescribed coefficients along the real path. We use the fixed circular row $$\\label{gauge:fixed-row}\n \\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g)\n   =\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}J\\,\\operatorname{pb}_J\\mathcal F_t(g).$$ In particular $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}$ is held fixed when this map is linearized at the possibly nonexact profile $g_0$. This circular row depends only on $\\xi$, so it preserves mean and oscillatory projections. All strip norms use the real parameter $\\xi$ after this pullback. Take $Y_0$ large. The map $\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}$ is analytic whenever $$\\frac{E^{-1/2}}{|r|^2}(W_m+W_o)\\ll1,\n \\qquad\n \\frac{E^{-1/2}}{|r|^2}W_o\\ll1,\n \\label{gauge:height-small}$$ where $v=g-g_0$ has mean and oscillation of $\\mathcal X_h(E)$ sizes $W_m,W_o$ respectively. Writing $W=W_m+W_o$, its remainder $\\mathcal N(v)=\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g_0+v)\n-\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g_0)-D\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g_0)v$ obeys $$\\|\\mathcal N(v)\\|_{\\mathcal Y_h}\n \\le C_h\\left(\\frac{E^{-1/2}}{|r|^2}W^2\n              +\\frac{E^{-1}}{|r|^4}W_o^2W\\right).\n \\label{gauge:height-bound}$$ With $A_r=E^{-1/2}/|r|^2$ and $C_r=E^{-1}/|r|^4$, its mean and oscillatory outputs satisfy, respectively, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|\\langle\\mathcal N(v)\\rangle\\|_{L^2_\\xi}\n       &\\le C_h\\{A_r(W_m^2+W_o^2)+C_rW_o^2W\\},\\notag\\\\\n \\|\\mathcal N(v)-\\langle\\mathcal N(v)\\rangle\\|_{\\mathcal Y_h}\n       &\\le C_h\\{A_r W_oW+C_rW_o^2W\\}.\n \\label{gauge:height-projections}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The corresponding multilinear difference estimates hold. These estimates are uniform at each fixed angular order.",

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lin-global",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an angular order $h$, a finite geometric parameter $D$, a cylindrical weight rate $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}>2.1$, and the compact observations from Lemma <a href=\"#lin:observations\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:observations\">5</a>. Consider surfaces of parameter size $B\\to\\infty$, obtained by replacing far cylindrical pieces by real-parameter paths with complex coefficients, optionally followed by height charts of length $O(\\log B)$. The conical ends may remain infinite. The following are the hypotheses on the linear operators and prescribed charts.*\n\n1.  *On each fixed compact subset, the coefficients, compact multiplier sources, and observations converge smoothly to <a href=\"#lin:augmented\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:augmented\">[lin:augmented]</a>, or to a member of a sufficiently small uniformly invertible perturbation of that block.*\n\n2.  *From a fixed entrance to $z=cB$, the cylindrical operator is a sufficiently small perturbation of <a href=\"#lin:cylinder-operator\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:cylinder-operator\">[lin:cylinder-operator]</a>. Choose $c>0$ so that a propagation rate $2.1$ is available. Beyond that point, bounded bands of length depending on $D$ satisfy Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>. A height chart is the real-parameter pullback of $\\tau=\\log(r_0/r)$, with $E\\asymp(B|r|)^{-2}$, ending with $B|r|\\ge Y_0$. Its coefficients obey the same accretivity, derivative, lower-term, and small-perturbation bounds.*\n\n3.  *Each modified cylindrical end has one ordered real outward interval $[s_0,T_B]$, equal to the original log coordinate on its long real part. Local real outward coordinates on overlaps are $t_i=\\chi_i(s)$ with $0<c\\le\\chi_i'\\le C$ and bounded required fixed derivatives; the real angular coordinate is unchanged. There is a positive scale $E_B(s)$ comparable to the local scales with bounded logarithmic derivatives. The prescribed scalar variables are descriptions of one scalar variable through transition factors $A_i(s,\\theta)$ on fixed overlap bands. The functions $A_i,A_i^{-1}$ and their ordinary real-coordinate derivatives through the required fixed orders are bounded. Choose this scalar variable to agree with each prescribed long-chart variable off those bands and with the prescribed exit variable near $T_B$. After these changes, the normalized reference operators and their source rows are smooth restrictions of one operator on the interval; any additional terms from the actual backgrounds satisfy the bounded lower-term and small domain-to-range perturbation hypotheses in (ii). These requirements exclude distributional seams. The coefficients on conical ends satisfy Lemma <a href=\"#lin:conical\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:conical\">9</a>, up to a small domain-to-range perturbation.*\n\n4.  *For each fixed $B$ and sufficiently remote finite stops on the conical ends, fixed domain and range isomorphisms identify the actual stopped operator with an operator connected to a real coercive scalar elliptic problem by an operator-norm continuous homotopy on the fixed compact $H^2$ domain with homogeneous boundary conditions and range $L^2$. Its coefficients and boundaries are smooth, its symbols are properly elliptic, and its boundary conditions are complementing throughout. The equal-dimensional compact observation and multiplier augmentation is retained. This is only an index hypothesis: the uniform estimates in the preceding items are required for the actual operators, not for the artificial operators along the homotopy.*\n\n\n*For clarity, the coefficient requirement in (iii) includes the tangent of every prescribed complex log path. If $t=t(s)$ is such a log and $H=t_s$ is its complex tangent, independent of $\\theta$, then the chain rule on the real $s$ interval gives $$\\label{lin:complex-log-pullback}\n \\begin{split}\n H\\mathcal L={}&\\partial_s-\\frac aH\\partial_{ss}\n       -2b\\partial_{s\\theta}-Hc\\partial_{\\theta\\theta}\\\\\n &+\\left(d_1+\\frac{aH_s}{H^2}\\right)\\partial_s\n       +Hd_2\\partial_\\theta+Hd_0,\n \\end{split}$$ and the source is multiplied by $H$. Thus $H,H^{-1}$ and its required fixed derivatives, including $H_s$, must be bounded. If the full drift is divided out, its divisor is $\\delta_H=1+d_1+aH_s/H^2$, and the actual inequalities in (ii) are $$\\operatorname{Re}\\frac{a}{H\\delta_H}\\ge cE_B,\\quad\n \\operatorname{Re}\\frac{Hc}{\\delta_H}\\ge c,\\quad\n \\left|\\frac{a}{H\\delta_H}\\right|\\le CE_B,\\quad\n \\left|\\frac{Hc}{\\delta_H}\\right|\\le C,\\quad\n \\left|\\frac b{\\delta_H}\\right|\\le\\varepsilon_*\\sqrt{E_B}.$$ The divided source is $Hf/\\delta_H$. A nonzero divisor alone does not imply these real-part inequalities. If $\\delta_H=1+O(E_B)$, its closeness to one preserves previously fixed strict margins.*\n\n*Choose a weight $\\rho_B$ with rate $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ on the long real cylinder, a sufficiently large fixed rate $d_D$ on the bounded modified bands, and a sufficiently large fixed rate $d_{\\mathrm{cap}}$ on a height chart, retaining its value at the entrance of each new chart. All rates exceed their propagation rates by fixed positive margins, are at least $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$, and their interpolations occupy fixed overlap bands where the adjacent coefficient estimates both hold. Choose $Y_0$ after these rates so that $d_{\\mathrm{cap}}\\sup E$ is sufficiently small; take $B$ large only after these choices.*\n\n\n*Here $u$ denotes the scalar unknown in each prescribed chart: normal height on the core, radius on cylindrical charts, relative height on cap charts, and link displacement on conical charts. The corresponding source uses the same change of graph units and drift normalization. Let $X_B$ consist of the compact norm <a href=\"#lin:compact-norm\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:compact-norm\">[lin:compact-norm]</a>, the cylindrical and height norms <a href=\"#lin:weighted-strip\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:weighted-strip\">[lin:weighted-strip]</a>, the conical norms <a href=\"#lin:conical-norm\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:conical-norm\">[lin:conical-norm]</a>, and the Euclidean norm of the compact multiplier vector. Let $Y_B$ consist of the corresponding compact and end source norms and the Euclidean observation norm. Homogeneous outgoing graph-derivative conditions are included in the domain. Then $$\\label{lin:global-estimate}\n \\|(u,\\lambda)\\|_{X_B}\n \\le C_{D,Y_0,h,\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}}\n \\left\\|\\bigl(L_Bu+\\sum_i\\lambda_i\\chi_{i,B},P_Bu\\bigr)\\right\\|_{Y_B},$$ and this normalized operator is onto. At a true terminal section define $g=u_s(T_B)$ for the prescribed scalar variable in the real outward coordinate. If $t=t(s)$ is a local log coordinate, this means $g=H u_t(T_B)$ with $H=t_s$. For this prescribed exit derivative the right hand side is augmented by $\\rho_B(T_B)^{-1}\\|g\\|_{\\mathcal T^N_{E(T_B),h}}$ at each terminal section; the sum over the fixed finite list of exits is understood. The thresholds and constant may depend on the fixed rate, but are independent of $B$ and of the lengths of the exhausted conical ends. Removing $\\rho_B$, or converting a relative height to physical height on a cap, costs at most a fixed power of $B$. The preliminary construction uses $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}=2.2$; a source with a fixed higher Taylor growth rate is permitted by choosing $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ equal to or larger than that rate. The strict buffer is above the propagation rate, so equality with the source growth rate is allowed in the uniformly local source norm.",

        "exact_quote": "On a fixed log-length overlap suppose the hypotheses of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a> hold with $E\\asymp B^{-2}$.         "anchor": "stmt-arr-real-stops",
        "exact_quote": "There are a fixed small complex $b$-neighborhood, $d_0>0$, and $H_0$ with the following property. For every independent stop length $H\\ge H_0$, stop each cylindrical end on its real path at height comparable to $H$, leaving the conical ends infinite. For $$b\\text{ in that neighborhood},\\qquad |x|<d_0H^{-2},$$ the normalized comparison problem has a solution $U_H(b,x)$, holomorphic in these finite parameters. In the analogue of $X_B$ with $B$ replaced by $H$, its correction from the base-plus-first-jet comparison pair is at most $C H^{-4}$. Thus the cylindrical strip bound is $C H^{-4}(1+z)^{2.2}$ and the compact and conical correction is $O(H^{-4})$. The paths and cutoffs are real and independent of the finite parameters, and the outgoing comparison derivatives are holomorphic in them. For real parameters the stopped surface is real.*\n\n\n*Let $F_H(b,x)$ be its Gaussian action. It is holomorphic and uniformly bounded on a fixed smaller polydisc.         "anchor": "stmt-arr-gevrey",
        "exact_quote": "For any sufficiently high real-coefficient polynomial path $p_0(s)$ with the specified opening jet and any sufficiently large fixed $\\ell$, the arrays $G_\\pm(s,p_0(s)+s^\\ell h)$, uniformly for $h$ in a fixed complex ball, have the formal stationary expansion of Gevrey order $1/k$. More precisely, if that expansion is $\\sum_{n\\ge0}f_n(h)s^n$, then $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|f_n\\|&\\le C A^n\\Gamma(1+n/k),\\label{arr:gevrey-coeff}\\\\\n \\left\\|G_\\pm(s,p_0(s)+s^\\ell h)\n      -\\sum_{n<N}f_n(h)s^n\\right\\|\n   &\\le C A^N\\Gamma(1+N/k)|s|^N\n       \\quad(N\\ge0).\\label{arr:gevrey-remainder}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The norm is the supremum on a fixed smaller $h$-ball. These statements hold also after any fixed finite number of parameter derivatives. The constants can depend on $D$.",
        "source_id": "PM-355.1"
      },

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-arr-gevrey",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-jump-jump",
        "exact_quote": "Let $G_+$ and $G_-$ be the two array actions at a common parameter $p$ in the inner parameter ball, and hence at common compact observation values, for a nonempty finite adverse end list with the same ordering of the bypasses on every end. Starting from these arrays, make the nonadverse synchronization <a href=\"#jump:nonadverse-sync\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"jump:nonadverse-sync\">[jump:nonadverse-sync]</a> and use the single normalized preliminary solution stopped at $T_{\\rm pre}$ above. Match $Z_{*,j}$ from that solution by <a href=\"#jump:matching-Z\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"jump:matching-Z\">[jump:matching-Z]</a>–<a href=\"#jump:scaling\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"jump:scaling\">[jump:scaling]</a>. The adverse continuations use the canonical profile $g_c$ and outgoing remainder derivatives $$\\psi=\\left.\\partial_s(g-g_c)\\right|_{\\mathrm{exit}}$$ in the natural Neumann trace class <a href=\"#jump:permitted-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"jump:permitted-data\">[jump:permitted-data]</a>, in the prescribed real path parameter at each exit. Let $Y_0$ be the fixed large exit cutoff for this class. The continuation at the first fixed radius interpolates the preliminary circular derivative and that of $g_c$ as in Proposition <a href=\"#jump:compatibility\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"jump:compatibility\">34</a>. The longer shrinking branches have $\\psi=0$ at their own exits, and the shorter interpolation uses their actual remainder traces at the common shorter section. Proposition <a href=\"#jump:compatibility\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"jump:compatibility\">34</a> proves membership in the relevant uniqueness balls and exact equality of the interpolation endpoints with the longer restrictions.*\n\n\n*For these actions there is a universal constant $\\mathfrak c\\ne0$ such that $$\\label{jump:action-jump}\n G_+-G_-=\\mathfrak c\n       \\sum_{j\\ \\mathrm{adverse}}\n       Z_{*,j}^{-2}e^{-Z_{*,j}^2/4}\n       +o\\left(\\sum_{j\\ \\mathrm{adverse}}\n                    |Z_{*,j}|^{-2}e^{-\\Re Z_{*,j}^2/4}\\right).$$ With $c_0$ defined by the upper-minus-lower $y^2$ lateral labels in Lemma <a href=\"#jump:stokes\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"jump:stokes\">37</a>, $\\mathfrak c=\\epsilon_{\\rm lab}8\\pi c_0$ for one common $\\epsilon_{\\rm lab}\\in\\{1,-1\\}$ determined by the array labels. Indeed an upper axial bypass in $z^2/Z_0^2$ becomes a lower $r^2$ bypass under $r^2=2(1-z^2/Z_0^2)$; this is one global label reversal, not an end-dependent sign. Reversing both array labels reverses $\\mathfrak c$. More precisely, the limsup of the relative error as $B\\to\\infty$ at fixed $Y_0$ is bounded by a quantity tending to zero as $Y_0\\to\\infty$.",
        "source_id": "PM-355.1"
      },

The adverse continuations use the canonical profile $g_c$ and outgoing remainder derivatives $$\\psi=\\left.\\partial_s(g-g_c)\\right|_{\\mathrm{exit}}$$ in the natural Neumann trace class <a href=\"#jump:permitted-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"jump:permitted-data\">[jump:permitted-data]</a>, in the prescribed real path parameter at each exit.         "exact_quote": "There are $\\theta\\in(0,1/2)$ and $\\gamma>0$ with the following property. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Fixed-center parabolic rescaling** ([source](#intro:rescalings)): For a singular point $(x_0,T)$ and a scale $\lambda>0$, define $$\label{intro:rescalings} M_s^\lambda=\lambda\bigl(M_{T+\lambda^{-2}s}-x_0\bigr),\qquad s<0,$$ whenever the original time belongs to $[0,T)$.
- **Backward integral Brakke tangent** ([source](#sec:introduction)): A *backward integral Brakke tangent* is a weakly measurable Radon family $(\mu_s)_{s<0}$ with the following properties. For almost every $s$, $\mu_s$ is the weight of an integral $2$-varifold $V_s$ with measurable generalized mean curvature $\mathbf H_\mu$ and first variation $\delta V_s=-\mathbf H_\mu\mu_s$ on compactly supported vector fields.
- **Self-shrinker and Gaussian area** ([source](#pm-h-3)): In the normalization used here, a self-shrinker $S$ satisfies $\mathbf H+X^\perp/2=0$ and generates the motion $\sqrt{-s}\,S$.
- **Gaussian action, stationary defect and dissipation** ([source](#sec:geometry)): We omit the inessential constant prefactor in the Gaussian area and put $$\label{geo:action} F(M)=\int_M e^{-\|X\|^2/4}\,\mathrm d\mu, \qquad \Phi=\mathbf H+\tfrac12X^\perp, \qquad d(\tau)^2=\int_{M(\tau)}\|\Phi\|^2e^{-\|X\|^2/4}\,\mathrm d\mu.$$
- **Gaussian Sobolev domain** ([source](#stmt-lin-gaussian)): Let $H^2_G$ be the completion of $C_c^\infty(S)$ for $$\\|u\\|_{H^2_G}=\sum_{i=0}^2\\|\nabla^iu\\|_{L^2_G}.$$
- **Compact observation** ([source](#sec:linear)): An observation means a real continuous linear functional $P_i u=\langle u,\chi_i\rangle_{L^2_G}$ with $\chi_i\in C_c^\infty(S)$.
- **Normalized stationary graph equation** ([source](#lin:normalized-equation)): We use the sign convention in which a normalized stationary graph satisfies $$\label{lin:normalized-equation} \Phi(u)+\sum_i\lambda_i\chi_i(u)=0,\qquad P(u)=q.$$
- **Cylindrical strip norm** ([source](#lin:strip-norm)): Fix an integer $h\ge4$. On a unit strip $I\times S^1$, with the diffusion scale $E(t)$ comparable to $E_I\in(0,E_*]$, define $$\label{lin:strip-norm} \begin{split} N_{E_I,h}(v;I)^2={}&\\|v\\|_{L^2H^h}^2+\\|v_t\\|_{L^2H^h}^2 +\\|v_{\theta\theta}\\|_{L^2H^h}^2\\ &+E_I^2\\|v_{tt}\\|_{L^2H^h}^2 +E_I\\|v_{t\theta}\\|_{L^2H^h}^2. \end{split}$$ Second derivatives in this definition are bulk $L^2$ quantities. The traces used below are traces of the function and its first derivatives, and do not include a trace of $v_{tt}$.
- **Weighted uniformly local cylindrical spaces** ([source](#lin:weighted-strip)): For a positive weight $\rho$ with bounded logarithmic derivatives, set $$\label{lin:weighted-strip} \\|v\\|_{X_{\rho,h}} =\sup_\nu\rho(t_\nu)^{-1}N_{E_\nu,h}(v;I_\nu),\qquad \\|f\\|_{Y_{\rho,h}} =\sup_\nu\rho(t_\nu)^{-1}\\|f\\|_{L^2(I_\nu;H^h)}.$$
- **Type-preserving and opening parameters** ([source](#pm-h-4)): Their parameters split as $(b,x)$. The analytic family at $x=0$ preserves end types, while $x$ has one quadratic opening coordinate for each cylindrical end.
- **Formal critical arc** ([source](#pm-h-4)): A formal critical arc is a tuple of real formal power series $(b(s),x(s))$, with zero constant terms, satisfying $\nabla\mathcal F(b(s),x(s))=0$ coefficient by coefficient.
- **Adverse end and leading action scale** ([source](#arr:A0)): On a chosen evaluation ray, call an end *adverse* when its leading opening $c_j a$ is negative real, so the circular profile $R_c(z)=\sqrt{2(1+\beta_j z^2)}$ reaches radius zero at a positive leading squared height $Z_{j,\mathrm{lead}}^2=(-c_j a)^{-1}$.
- **Complete graphical intersection** ([source](#sec:localized)): For precision, a complete graph on a ball means that the *entire* intersection of the surface with that ball is given by the indicated single graph: no further component or sheet is permitted.
- **Localized defect parameter** ([source](#sec:localized)): Put $$\label{flow:D} \mathcal D=\\|\Phi_M\\|_{L^2_G(M)} +e^{-(1-\eta)R^2/8}.$$
- **Delayed graphical radii** ([source](#flow:radii)): For each unit interval wholly available in the bootstrap put $$\label{flow:radii} \begin{gathered} a_j=(\mathcal E(j)-\mathcal E(j+1))^{1/2},\quad r_j=\sqrt{8\log(1/a_j)},\\ R_j=\min\left\{Q^jR_{\rm in}, \min_{0\le i\le j}Q^{j-i}r_i\right\}. \end{gathered}$$

The prescribed scalar variables are descriptions of one scalar variable through transition factors $A_i(s,\\theta)$ on fixed overlap bands. The functions $A_i,A_i^{-1}$ and their ordinary real-coordinate derivatives through the required fixed orders are bounded. Choose this scalar variable to agree with each prescribed long-chart variable off those bands and with the prescribed exit variable near $T_B$. After these changes, the normalized reference operators and their source rows are smooth restrictions of one operator on the interval; any additional terms from the actual backgrounds satisfy the bounded lower-term and small domain-to-range perturbation hypotheses in (ii). These requirements exclude distributional seams. The coefficients on conical ends satisfy Lemma <a href=\"#lin:conical\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:conical\">9</a>, up to a small domain-to-range perturbation.* 4. *For each fixed $B$ and sufficiently remote finite stops on the conical ends, fixed domain and range isomorphisms identify the actual stopped operator with an operator connected to a real coercive scalar elliptic problem by an operator-norm continuous homotopy on the fixed compact $H^2$ domain with homogeneous boundary conditions and range $L^2$. Its coefficients and boundaries are smooth, its symbols are properly elliptic, and its boundary conditions are complementing throughout. The equal-dimensional compact observation and multiplier augmentation is retained. This is only an index hypothesis: the uniform estimates in the preceding items are required for the actual operators, not for the artificial operators along the homotopy.* *For clarity, the coefficient requirement in (iii) includes the tangent of every prescribed complex log path. If $t=t(s)$ is such a log and $H=t_s$ is its complex tangent, independent of $\\theta$, then the chain rule on the real $s$ interval gives $$\\label{lin:complex-log-pullback} \\begin{split} H\\mathcal L={}&\\partial_s-\\frac aH\\partial_{ss} -2b\\partial_{s\\theta}-Hc\\partial_{\\theta\\theta}\\\\ &+\\left(d_1+\\frac{aH_s}{H^2}\\right)\\partial_s +Hd_2\\partial_\\theta+Hd_0, \\end{split}$$ and the source is multiplied by $H$. Thus $H,H^{-1}$ and its required fixed derivatives, including $H_s$, must be bounded. If the full drift is divided out, its divisor is $\\delta_H=1+d_1+aH_s/H^2$, and the actual inequalities in (ii) are $$\\operatorname{Re}\\frac{a}{H\\delta_H}\\ge cE_B,\\quad \\operatorname{Re}\\frac{Hc}{\\delta_H}\\ge c,\\quad \\left|\\frac{a}{H\\delta_H}\\right|\\le CE_B,\\quad \\left|\\frac{Hc}{\\delta_H}\\right|\\le C,\\quad \\left|\\frac b{\\delta_H}\\right|\\le\\varepsilon_*\\sqrt{E_B}.$$ The divided source is $Hf/\\delta_H$. A nonzero divisor alone does not imply these real-part inequalities. If $\\delta_H=1+O(E_B)$, its closeness to one preserves previously fixed strict margins.* *Choose a weight $\\rho_B$ with rate $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ on the long real cylinder, a sufficiently large fixed rate $d_D$ on the bounded modified bands, and a sufficiently large fixed rate $d_{\\mathrm{cap}}$ on a height chart, retaining its value at the entrance of each new chart. All rates exceed their propagation rates by fixed positive margins, are at least $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$, and their interpolations occupy fixed overlap bands where the adjacent coefficient estimates both hold. Choose $Y_0$ after these rates so that $d_{\\mathrm{cap}}\\sup E$ is sufficiently small; take $B$ large only after these choices.* *Here $u$ denotes the scalar unknown in each prescribed chart: normal height on the core, radius on cylindrical charts, relative height on cap charts, and link displacement on conical charts. The corresponding source uses the same change of graph units and drift normalization. Let $X_B$ consist of the compact norm <a href=\"#lin:compact-norm\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:compact-norm\">[lin:compact-norm]</a>, the cylindrical and height norms <a href=\"#lin:weighted-strip\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:weighted-strip\">[lin:weighted-strip]</a>, the conical norms <a href=\"#lin:conical-norm\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:conical-norm\">[lin:conical-norm]</a>, and the Euclidean norm of the compact multiplier vector. Let $Y_B$ consist of the corresponding compact and end source norms and the Euclidean observation norm. Homogeneous outgoing graph-derivative conditions are included in the domain. Then $$\\label{lin:global-estimate} \\|(u,\\lambda)\\|_{X_B} \\le C_{D,Y_0,h,\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}} \\left\\|\\bigl(L_Bu+\\sum_i\\lambda_i\\chi_{i,B},P_Bu\\bigr)\\right\\|_{Y_B},$$ and this normalized operator is onto. At a true terminal section define $g=u_s(T_B)$ for the prescribed scalar variable in the real outward coordinate. If $t=t(s)$ is a local log coordinate, this means $g=H u_t(T_B)$ with $H=t_s$. For this prescribed exit derivative the right hand side is augmented by $\\rho_B(T_B)^{-1}\\|g\\|_{\\mathcal T^N_{E(T_B),h}}$ at each terminal section; the sum over the fixed finite list of exits is understood. The thresholds and constant may depend on the fixed rate, but are independent of $B$ and of the lengths of the exhausted conical ends. Removing $\\rho_B$, or converting a relative height to physical height on a cap, costs at most a fixed power of $B$. The preliminary construction uses $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}=2.2$; a source with a fixed higher Taylor growth rate is permitted by choosing $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ equal to or larger than that rate. Put $$\\label{flow:D}\n \\mathcal D=\\|\\Phi_M\\|_{L^2_G(M)}\n              +e^{-(1-\\eta)R^2/8}.$$ Then $$\\label{flow:localized-conclusions}\n |F(M)-F(S)|^{1-\\theta}\\le C_\\eta\\mathcal D,\n \\qquad |x|\\le C_\\eta\\mathcal D^\\gamma .$$ For each fixed compact reference region $K$, transported to $K_b\\subset\nS_b$ by the family charts, there are $R_{\\eta,K}\\ge R_\\eta$ and $C_{\\eta,K}<\\infty$ such that, when $R\\ge R_{\\eta,K}$, the normal height $u$ of $M$ satisfies $$\\label{flow:compact-height}\n \\|u\\|_{H^2(K_b)}\\le C_{\\eta,K}\n        (\\mathcal D+\\mathcal D^\\gamma).$$ When $\\mathcal D\\le1$, the right side can be replaced by $C_{\\eta,K}\\mathcal D^\\gamma$. <a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-representative-equality** [claim](#stmt-geo-representative) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geo-representative): Subtract compact-test transport identities and sandwich exceptional slices between good times. -> Equality of every interior-time Radon measure.
- **step-tangent-geometry** [claim](#stmt-geo-tangent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geo-tangent): Use multiplicity-one compactness and vanishing density drop, then apply the end structure theorem. -> Smooth tangent section with separated conical and cylindrical ends.
- **step-gaussian-domain** [claim](#stmt-lin-gaussian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-gaussian): Combine weighted moment integrations with half-density conjugation and compactness on exhausted domains. -> Gaussian domain estimate, compact resolvent and finite-dimensional kernel.
- **step-observation-block** [claim](#stmt-lin-observations) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-observations): Separate the kernel and enlarge compact source pairings by a finite nondegenerate symmetric extension. -> Invertible augmented block with the required normalized variations.
- **step-strip-inverse** [claim](#stmt-lin-strip) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-strip): Freeze coefficients, estimate Fourier symbols and boundary roots, then absorb commutators. -> Bulk estimates and natural first-derivative boundary traces.
- **step-radial-map** [claim](#stmt-gauge-radial) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gauge-radial): Invert the radial graph metric and apply analytic algebra-module product estimates. -> Analytic radial map with a small mean-value perturbation.
- **step-cylindrical-rates** [claim](#stmt-lin-rates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-rates): Separate slow Fourier channels from the fast derivative inverse and improve the nonlinear tail before using normalized decay. -> Cylindrical remainder decay and opening and tilt asymptotics.
- **step-conical-inverse** [claim](#stmt-lin-conical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-conical): Use complementary weighted energy multipliers, angular commutation and exhaustion with terminal terms retained. -> Uniform conical Dirichlet inverse and boundary estimates.
- **step-conical-gaussian-identification** [claim](#stmt-lin-gaussian-conical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-gaussian-conical): Lift the conical entrance solution into the Gaussian domain and identify it by a real-operator maximum principle. -> Conical-domain membership of Gaussian Jacobi solutions.
- **step-fiber-chart** [claim](#stmt-gauge-fiber-atlas) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gauge-fiber-atlas): Interpolate transverse ambient fiber maps with a partition on the fixed real base. -> A unified chart analytic in the finite parameters.
- **step-compact-conical-maps** [claim](#stmt-gauge-compact) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gauge-compact): Keep the highest derivative in the bulk module and estimate compact coefficients in commuting flow boxes. -> Analytic conical and compact nonlinear maps.
- **step-family-and-jets** [claim](#stmt-lin-family) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-family): Apply the type-preserving implicit inverse, construct opening coefficients successively and integrate action coefficients using Gaussian domination. -> Analytic base family, formal polynomial-growth opening jets and formal Gaussian action.
- **step-shifted-comparison** [claim](#stmt-lin-shifted-gaussian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-shifted-gaussian): Conjugate the uniformly perturbed half-density inverse back to the shifted real Gaussian measure. -> Shifted Gaussian comparison including compact multiplier derivatives.
- **step-finite-taylor-graphs** [claim](#stmt-ref-finite-taylor) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ref-finite-taylor): Convert finite jets coefficientwise to real normal heights and cut off beyond a polynomial radius. -> Globally small Taylor graphs and controlled equation, action and observation errors.
- **step-real-local-comparison** [claim](#stmt-ref-real-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ref-real-comparison): Subtract the normalized equations, retain actual principal coefficients and apply the augmented cutoff estimate. -> Local height and multiplier comparison with a separate omitted-action estimate.
- **step-lateral-contours** [claim](#stmt-arr-contours) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-contours): Construct strict circle and ray profiles, then deform through admissible squared-height profiles. -> Upper and lower bypasses and the required shortening homotopies.
- **step-mixed-gauge** [claim](#stmt-gauge-mixed) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gauge-mixed): Use exact determinant and Schur-complement cancellations before estimating coefficient modules. -> Full mixed-gauge nonlinear and mean-curve estimates.
- **step-height-gauge** [claim](#stmt-gauge-height) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gauge-height): Normalize polar slopes, retain graph-dependent drift division and split mean and oscillatory products. -> Analytic long-height map and projected remainder estimates.
- **step-global-weighted-inverse** [claim](#stmt-lin-global) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-global): Prove a single weighted exterior estimate, exclude escape by a compact-limit argument and use stopped index zero for surjectivity. -> Uniform weighted normalized inverse with polynomial physical conversion losses.
- **step-backward-shielding** [claim](#stmt-lin-shielding) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lin-shielding): Conjugate by a large positive exponential and keep the actual Robin exit and shifted derivative slots. -> Exponential suppression on earlier bands.
- **step-preliminary-arrays** [claim](#stmt-arr-preliminary-solves) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-preliminary-solves): Correct the base-plus-first-jet circular comparison using the uniform weighted inverse and a contraction with independent trace lifts. -> Exact normalized preliminary arrays and joint parameter-trace holomorphy.
- **step-endpoint-variation** [claim](#stmt-arr-first-variation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-first-variation): Differentiate the Gaussian density on moving domains and retain both boundary momentum and position terms. -> Exponential endpoint and antiholomorphic action estimates.
- **step-real-stopped-disks** [claim](#stmt-arr-real-stops) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-real-stops): Solve independent real stopped problems on shrinking opening polydiscs and compare consecutive stops by endpoint variation. -> Full-disk action approximants with exponentially small successive differences.
- **step-gevrey-telescope** [claim](#stmt-arr-gevrey) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-gevrey): Telescope geometric stopping scales, estimate coefficient moments and identify coefficients by real finite Taylor comparison. -> Formal stationary Gevrey coefficients and all-orders remainders.
- **step-fixed-division-closure** [claim](#stmt-arr-division) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-division): Subtract low Taylor jets before division and compare uniformly contracting implicit roots of disk approximants. -> Closure under analytic operations, fixed division and regular implicit solution.
- **step-adic-replacement** [claim](#stmt-arr-formal-replacement) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-formal-replacement): Select maximal gradient rank and use cofactor tangent derivations with explicit denominator valuations. -> Adically valid polynomial replacement retaining every original constraint.
- **step-sector-implicit-curves** [claim](#stmt-arr-regular-implicit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-regular-implicit): Normalize the selected subsystem by fixed powers and its minor, then apply regular implicit contraction and antiholomorphic chain rules. -> Sectorial parameter selections with flat original constraints.
- **step-flatness-upgrade** [claim](#stmt-arr-flatness-upgrade) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-flatness-upgrade): Remove the antiholomorphic source by a bounded Cauchy transform and apply a sector maximum principle. -> Improved exponential decay on the evaluation ray.
- **step-common-parameter-upper** [claim](#stmt-arr-action-upper) / [proof](#proof-stmt-arr-action-upper): Compare implicit roots and Taylor-transport both actions to their midpoint with a strict quadratic exponential margin. -> Common-parameter upper bound, also on nearby generic complex rays.
- **step-height-inverse** [claim](#stmt-jump-height-inverse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jump-height-inverse): Retain the finite mean kernel and its terminal layer, and use an angular spectral buffer for oscillation. -> Separate finite-height inverse estimates for mean and oscillatory components.
- **step-height-compatibility** [claim](#stmt-jump-compatibility) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jump-compatibility): Solve in projected exterior weights, shield and splice to the preliminary core, then identify restrictions inside augmented uniqueness balls. -> Compatible normalized height families with exact restriction endpoints and retained multipliers.
- **step-moving-exit** [claim](#stmt-jump-moving-exit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jump-moving-exit): Differentiate pulled equations with homogeneous remainder exit conditions and shield the differentiated splice residual. -> Physical moving-boundary estimate in the small exterior scale.
- **step-exterior-limit-and-endpoint-cost** [claim](#stmt-jump-endpoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jump-endpoints): Pass to compact scaled height limits and integrate boundary variations using the Gaussian gap. -> Radial translator limits and a small relative action cost of shortening.
- **step-nonzero-stokes** [claim](#stmt-jump-stokes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jump-stokes): Construct lateral solutions by directional Volterra contraction, prove factorial remainders and contradict lateral agreement using positive Borel coefficients. -> A common nonzero lateral slope-jump coefficient and finite-bypass comparison.
- **step-universal-action-jump** [claim](#stmt-jump-jump) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jump-stokes-2): Use exact finite-scale first variation before taking limits, cancel boundary height momentum and compare lateral slopes. -> Universal signed action jump summed over absolute adverse-end scales.
- **step-mean-opening-jets** [claim](#stmt-phase-jets) / [proof](#proof-stmt-phase-jets): Derive the exact radial equation, exploit its angular divergence and extract the resonant slow mean coefficient by Gaussian flux. -> Improved jet growth and the quadratic mean logarithm.
- **step-inner-mean** [claim](#stmt-phase-inner-evaluation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-phase-inner-evaluation): Use a retained Taylor-weight forced inverse and a separately shielded remote boundary lift. -> Incoming mean evaluation with the precision needed for constant-order phase matching.
- **step-averaged-primitive** [claim](#stmt-phase-primitive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-phase-primitive): Average in the prescribed gauges and integrate the exact circular equation with a bulk derivative budget. -> Integrated mean equation with negligible accumulated phase error.
- **step-constant-order-phase** [claim](#stmt-phase-expansion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-phase-expansion): Integrate the explicit mean primitive, match the height section and evaluate the correction antiderivative. -> Shifted exterior squared height through constant order with a universal logarithmic coefficient.
- **step-exclude-opening-arcs** [claim](#stmt-phase-no-arc) / [proof](#proof-stmt-phase-no-arc): Choose a generic nearby evaluation ray, separate Laurent principal parts and use positive tied relative weights to contradict the upper bound. -> Every real formal critical arc has vanishing openings.
- **step-finite-power-certificates** [claim](#stmt-jet-finite-power) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jet-finite-power): Apply the formal real arc criterion, reduce finite certificate quotients and use analytic approximation before evaluating real sums of squares. -> A fixed opening exponent valid for sufficiently high action truncations.
- **step-localized-gradient** [claim](#stmt-flow-localized) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-localized): Compare an actual slice with one fixed Taylor graph, absorb opening remainders and combine an analytic gradient inequality with Gaussian interpolation. -> Localized gradient, opening, compact-height and multiplier estimates.
- **step-elliptic-improvement** [claim](#stmt-flow-improvement) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-improvement): Convert the Gaussian defect bound to interior forcing control and compare exterior heights with polynomial and exponential supersolutions. -> Small height and slope on a smaller ball and small compact multipliers.
- **step-complete-graph-propagation** [claim](#stmt-flow-propagation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-propagation): Combine whole-intersection pseudolocality, avoidance confinement, normal-projection coverage and positive-time graphical smoothing. -> Uniform finite comparison and derivative control after positive delay.
- **step-radius-induction** [claim](#stmt-flow-radius-induction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-radius-induction): Improve the current slice, propagate and smooth, pay the observation-driven base-chart change, then apply the next localized estimate. -> Valid complete graphical hypotheses at every available selected slice.
- **step-finite-prefix-length** [claim](#stmt-flow-finite-length) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-finite-length): Split indices by tail size, use concavity for good indices and absorb the historical bad-index convolution. -> A uniform finite-prefix length bound.
- **step-fixed-frame-convergence** [claim](#stmt-flow-uniqueness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-uniqueness): Close the bootstrap using finite-prefix length, prove radius divergence and propagate from preceding slices with positive delay. -> Smooth fixed-frame convergence at all rescaled times.
- **step-main-and-weak-tangent-conclusion** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-flow-uniqueness-3): Restore the exact negative-time rescaling identity, identify extracted spacetime weights and apply all-endpoint representative equality. -> Full-family convergence and equality of every negative-time tangent measure at each first singular point.

Moreover $$\\label{lin:first-traces}\n \\sup_{t\\in I}\\bigl(\\|v(t)\\|_{H^h}\n +\\|v_\\theta(t)\\|_{H^h}+\\sqrt{E_I}\\|v_t(t)\\|_{H^h}\\bigr)\n \\le C N_{E_I,h}(v;I^+).$$ For inhomogeneous boundary data one can use the spaces $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|\\varphi\\|_{\\mathcal T^{D}_{E,h}}^2\n &=\\sum_{j\\in\\mathbb Z}(1+j^2)^h(1+j^2)\n                  (1+\\sqrt E|j|)|\\varphi_j|^2,\n       \\label{lin:dirichlet-trace}\\\\\n \\|\\psi\\|_{\\mathcal T^{N}_{E,h}}^2\n &=E\\sum_{j\\in\\mathbb Z}(1+j^2)^h\n                  (1+\\sqrt E|j|)|\\psi_j|^2.\n       \\label{lin:neumann-trace}\n\\end{aligned}$$ They are bounded by the bulk norm for $\\varphi=v|_{\\partial I}$ and $\\psi=v_t|_{\\partial I}$.           "anchor": "stmt-lin-rates",
          "exact_quote": "For <a href=\"#lin:cylinder-operator\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:cylinder-operator\">[lin:cylinder-operator]</a>, and for perturbations satisfying the normalized decay condition below, a weight $e^{\\alpha t}$ with $\\alpha\\notin\\{2-j^2:j\\in\\mathbb Z\\}$ gives separated end estimates. Slow data of rate below $\\alpha$ are prescribed at the entrance; slow data of rate above $\\alpha$ are prescribed at infinity (or at the appropriate finite exit). Finite intervals have logarithmic length at least a fixed $\\ell_*>0$, with constants allowed to depend on $\\ell_*$. Estimates hold with every fixed number of log-coordinate derivatives when the source has the corresponding regularity, with an arbitrarily small loss in a stated polynomial power.*\n\n\n*Here the second-order differential perturbation $Q=\\mathcal L-\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ retains the strict principal accretivity of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>, with $E\\asymp e^{-2t}$, and, for the chosen $0<\\eta<1$, has the following gain on every fixed weight used in the assertion: $$\\label{lin:normalized-decay}\n \\|Qv\\|_{Y_{e^{(\\beta-2+\\eta)t},h}}\n       \\le C_{\\beta,h,\\eta}\\|v\\|_{X_{e^{\\beta t},h}}.$$ The analogous bound is required after the fixed translations and commutations used to obtain derivative estimates. Thus the changes of the radial, mixed, and angular principal coefficients are measured in their respective units $E$, $\\sqrt E$, and $1$; lower coefficient terms may instead be measured in the corresponding coefficient–module operator norm. Ordinary absolute decay of the radial coefficient is not the condition in <a href=\"#lin:normalized-decay\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:normalized-decay\">[lin:normalized-decay]</a>.*\n\n\n*Consequently, on each cylindrical end and for every small $\\eta>0$, $$\\label{lin:end-expansion}\n R-\\sqrt2=O(z^{-2+\\eta}),\\qquad\n J=c z^2+z(\\ell\\cdot e_r)+O(z^\\eta)$$ for a Gaussian Jacobi solution with compact source. If $c=0$, subtracting the exact infinitesimal rotation with tilt $\\ell$ leaves $O(z^{-2+\\eta})$.           "exact_quote": "Let $\\kappa$ be the number of cylindrical ends. For real $b$, their coefficientwise conversions to normal graph jets are smooth in $b$ and have uniform polynomial bounds at every fixed derivative order. In particular $\\beta$ is exactly homogeneous linear in $x$ for fixed $b$.*\n\n\n3.  *Integrating the Gaussian action coefficient by coefficient defines $\\mathcal F\\in\\mathbb R\\{b\\}[[x]]$, with $$\\label{lin:action-multipliers}\n      \\nabla_p\\mathcal F=(D_p\\mathsf P)^{\\mathsf T}\\lambda.$$ Every fixed truncation of the prescribed graph series and every fixed number of its parameter or spatial derivatives has uniform polynomial end bounds on a sufficiently small complex $b$ neighborhood. The real normal truncations have the analogous smooth bounds for real parameters.           "exact_quote": "For every fixed $M\\ge1$, let $v^{(M)}(b,x)$ be the coefficientwise real normal-height polynomial through degree $M$ in the opening variables, let $\\lambda_M$ be the multiplier polynomial, and let $f_M$ be the same truncation of $\\mathcal F$. For an arbitrary real multiplier $\\lambda_U$, put $$r_U=\\mathcal N_b(u,\\lambda_U),\\qquad\n e_P=P(u)-\\mathsf P(p),\\qquad\n w=\\chi_R(u-v),\\qquad \\ell=\\lambda_U-\\lambda_M,$$ and define the annular error $$\\mathfrak a_R=\n \\left\\|(1+|Y|)|\\nabla(u-v)|+(1+|Y|)^2|u-v|\n \\right\\|_{L^2_a(\\{\\vartheta R<|Y|<R\\})}.$$ Then $$\\label{ref:real-comparison-estimate}\n \\|w\\|_{\\mathcal H^2_a}+|\\ell|\n \\le C_{M,\\vartheta}\\left(\\|\\chi_R r_U\\|_{L^2_a}+|e_P|\n                    +|x|^{M+1}+\\mathfrak a_R\\right).$$ The constants are uniform for $b$ in the fixed closed real neighborhood.           "exact_quote": "Let $B\\ge1$ and, on a bounded interval, prescribe smooth circular reference functions and transverse coefficients $$X(t,\\theta)=(B\\zeta(t,\\theta),R(t,\\theta)e_r(\\theta)),\\quad\n \\zeta=\\zeta_0+c_1u,\\qquad R=R_0+c_2u.\n \\label{gauge:immersion}$$ Assume that $R_0$, $\\zeta_0'$ and $c_2\\zeta_0'-c_1R_0'$ are bounded away from zero, that their required fixed derivatives are bounded, and that the circular reference has the strict ellipticity margins of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a> after division by its drift. Constants may depend on these fixed margins. Then the scalar stationary operator divided by the normal component of $X_u$ is an analytic map from a sufficiently small $\\mathcal X_h(B^{-2})$ ball to $\\mathcal Y_h$. If $\\|u\\|_{\\mathcal X_h(B^{-2})}\\le W$ and $BW$ is sufficiently small, its nonlinear remainder satisfies $$\\|\\mathcal Q(u)-\\mathcal Q(0)-D\\mathcal Q(0)u\\|_{\\mathcal Y_h}\n       \\le C_h(BW^2+B^2W^3).\n \\label{gauge:mixed-bound}$$ On that ball its Lipschitz constant, after subtraction of the linear part, is at most $C_h(BW+B^2W^2)$. Averaging the equation in these prescribed coordinates gives the same bound for the defect of the circular mean curve. These statements include all angular commutations through order $h$.",
          "source_id": "PM-355.1"
        }

          "exact_quote": "Prescribe the polar height chart $$X=(Zg(r,\\theta),r e_r(\\theta))$$ on real parameters along a fixed complex $r$ contour. Assume $|Br|\\ge Y_0$ and put $E=|Br|^{-2}$ on each strip. The reference conditions include the full real pullback and drift division. More precisely, if $t=t(\\xi)$ on the real outward parameter and $J=t_\\xi$, assume $J,J^{-1}$ and their required fixed derivatives are bounded. Let $\\mathcal F_t(g)$ denote the left side of the log-normalized equation <a href=\"#gauge:polar-normalized\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"gauge:polar-normalized\">[gauge:polar-normalized]</a> below, including its graph-dependent $H_1$ division. Write its circular linearization in the log coordinate as $$D\\mathcal F_t(g_0)v=(1+d_{\\mathrm{ref}})v_t-a_{\\mathrm{ref}}v_{tt}\n       -c_{\\mathrm{ref}}v_{\\theta\\theta}+q_{\\mathrm{ref}}v.$$ Its full pulled drift is $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}=1+d_{\\mathrm{ref}}\n             +a_{\\mathrm{ref}}J_\\xi/J^2$. Assume this is a bounded unit and that, after division by it, $$\\operatorname{Re}\\frac{a_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{J\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\ge cE,\n \\quad \\left|\\frac{a_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{J\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\right|\\le CE,\n \\quad \\operatorname{Re}\\frac{Jc_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\ge c,\n \\quad \\left|\\frac{Jc_{\\mathrm{ref}}}{\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}}\\right|\\le C.$$ The normalized coefficient derivatives and lower terms satisfy the bounds of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>. All metric and graph denominators in $\\mathcal F_t$ remain bounded analytic units in their normalized scales on the graph neighborhood. These are algebraic hypotheses on the prescribed reference, checked for the collapsing paths below. Let $\\operatorname{pb}_J$ mean the algebraic pullback obtained by replacing $\\partial_t$ with $J^{-1}\\partial_\\xi$ and reading all prescribed coefficients along the real path. We use the fixed circular row $$\\label{gauge:fixed-row}\n \\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g)\n   =\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}J\\,\\operatorname{pb}_J\\mathcal F_t(g).$$ In particular $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{ref}}$ is held fixed when this map is linearized at the possibly nonexact profile $g_0$. This circular row depends only on $\\xi$, so it preserves mean and oscillatory projections. All strip norms use the real parameter $\\xi$ after this pullback. Take $Y_0$ large. The map $\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}$ is analytic whenever $$\\frac{E^{-1/2}}{|r|^2}(W_m+W_o)\\ll1,\n \\qquad\n \\frac{E^{-1/2}}{|r|^2}W_o\\ll1,\n \\label{gauge:height-small}$$ where $v=g-g_0$ has mean and oscillation of $\\mathcal X_h(E)$ sizes $W_m,W_o$ respectively. Writing $W=W_m+W_o$, its remainder $\\mathcal N(v)=\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g_0+v)\n-\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g_0)-D\\mathcal F_{\\mathrm{norm}}(g_0)v$ obeys $$\\|\\mathcal N(v)\\|_{\\mathcal Y_h}\n \\le C_h\\left(\\frac{E^{-1/2}}{|r|^2}W^2\n              +\\frac{E^{-1}}{|r|^4}W_o^2W\\right).\n \\label{gauge:height-bound}$$ With $A_r=E^{-1/2}/|r|^2$ and $C_r=E^{-1}/|r|^4$, its mean and oscillatory outputs satisfy, respectively, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|\\langle\\mathcal N(v)\\rangle\\|_{L^2_\\xi}\n       &\\le C_h\\{A_r(W_m^2+W_o^2)+C_rW_o^2W\\},\\notag\\\\\n \\|\\mathcal N(v)-\\langle\\mathcal N(v)\\rangle\\|_{\\mathcal Y_h}\n       &\\le C_h\\{A_r W_oW+C_rW_o^2W\\}.\n \\label{gauge:height-projections}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The corresponding multilinear difference estimates hold. These estimates are uniform at each fixed angular order.",

          "anchor": "stmt-lin-global",
          "exact_quote": "Fix an angular order $h$, a finite geometric parameter $D$, a cylindrical weight rate $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}>2.1$, and the compact observations from Lemma <a href=\"#lin:observations\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:observations\">5</a>. Choose $c>0$ so that a propagation rate $2.1$ is available. Beyond that point, bounded bands of length depending on $D$ satisfy Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>. A height chart is the real-parameter pullback of $\\tau=\\log(r_0/r)$, with $E\\asymp(B|r|)^{-2}$, ending with $B|r|\\ge Y_0$. Its coefficients obey the same accretivity, derivative, lower-term, and small-perturbation bounds.*\n\n3.  *Each modified cylindrical end has one ordered real outward interval $[s_0,T_B]$, equal to the original log coordinate on its long real part. Local real outward coordinates on overlaps are $t_i=\\chi_i(s)$ with $0<c\\le\\chi_i'\\le C$ and bounded required fixed derivatives; the real angular coordinate is unchanged. There is a positive scale $E_B(s)$ comparable to the local scales with bounded logarithmic derivatives. The prescribed scalar variables are descriptions of one scalar variable through transition factors $A_i(s,\\theta)$ on fixed overlap bands. The functions $A_i,A_i^{-1}$ and their ordinary real-coordinate derivatives through the required fixed orders are bounded. Choose this scalar variable to agree with each prescribed long-chart variable off those bands and with the prescribed exit variable near $T_B$. After these changes, the normalized reference operators and their source rows are smooth restrictions of one operator on the interval; any additional terms from the actual backgrounds satisfy the bounded lower-term and small domain-to-range perturbation hypotheses in (ii). These requirements exclude distributional seams. The coefficients on conical ends satisfy Lemma <a href=\"#lin:conical\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:conical\">9</a>, up to a small domain-to-range perturbation.*\n\n4.  *For each fixed $B$ and sufficiently remote finite stops on the conical ends, fixed domain and range isomorphisms identify the actual stopped operator with an operator connected to a real coercive scalar elliptic problem by an operator-norm continuous homotopy on the fixed compact $H^2$ domain with homogeneous boundary conditions and range $L^2$. Its coefficients and boundaries are smooth, its symbols are properly elliptic, and its boundary conditions are complementing throughout. The equal-dimensional compact observation and multiplier augmentation is retained. This is only an index hypothesis: the uniform estimates in the preceding items are required for the actual operators, not for the artificial operators along the homotopy.*\n\n\n*For clarity, the coefficient requirement in (iii) includes the tangent of every prescribed complex log path. If $t=t(s)$ is such a log and $H=t_s$ is its complex tangent, independent of $\\theta$, then the chain rule on the real $s$ interval gives $$\\label{lin:complex-log-pullback}\n \\begin{split}\n H\\mathcal L={}&\\partial_s-\\frac aH\\partial_{ss}\n       -2b\\partial_{s\\theta}-Hc\\partial_{\\theta\\theta}\\\\\n &+\\left(d_1+\\frac{aH_s}{H^2}\\right)\\partial_s\n       +Hd_2\\partial_\\theta+Hd_0,\n \\end{split}$$ and the source is multiplied by $H$. Thus $H,H^{-1}$ and its required fixed derivatives, including $H_s$, must be bounded. If the full drift is divided out, its divisor is $\\delta_H=1+d_1+aH_s/H^2$, and the actual inequalities in (ii) are $$\\operatorname{Re}\\frac{a}{H\\delta_H}\\ge cE_B,\\quad\n \\operatorname{Re}\\frac{Hc}{\\delta_H}\\ge c,\\quad\n \\left|\\frac{a}{H\\delta_H}\\right|\\le CE_B,\\quad\n \\left|\\frac{Hc}{\\delta_H}\\right|\\le C,\\quad\n \\left|\\frac b{\\delta_H}\\right|\\le\\varepsilon_*\\sqrt{E_B}.$$ The divided source is $Hf/\\delta_H$. A nonzero divisor alone does not imply these real-part inequalities. If $\\delta_H=1+O(E_B)$, its closeness to one preserves previously fixed strict margins.*\n\n*Choose a weight $\\rho_B$ with rate $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ on the long real cylinder, a sufficiently large fixed rate $d_D$ on the bounded modified bands, and a sufficiently large fixed rate $d_{\\mathrm{cap}}$ on a height chart, retaining its value at the entrance of each new chart. All rates exceed their propagation rates by fixed positive margins, are at least $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$, and their interpolations occupy fixed overlap bands where the adjacent coefficient estimates both hold. Choose $Y_0$ after these rates so that $d_{\\mathrm{cap}}\\sup E$ is sufficiently small; take $B$ large only after these choices.*\n\n\n*Here $u$ denotes the scalar unknown in each prescribed chart: normal height on the core, radius on cylindrical charts, relative height on cap charts, and link displacement on conical charts. The corresponding source uses the same change of graph units and drift normalization. Let $X_B$ consist of the compact norm <a href=\"#lin:compact-norm\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:compact-norm\">[lin:compact-norm]</a>, the cylindrical and height norms <a href=\"#lin:weighted-strip\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:weighted-strip\">[lin:weighted-strip]</a>, the conical norms <a href=\"#lin:conical-norm\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:conical-norm\">[lin:conical-norm]</a>, and the Euclidean norm of the compact multiplier vector. Let $Y_B$ consist of the corresponding compact and end source norms and the Euclidean observation norm. Homogeneous outgoing graph-derivative conditions are included in the domain. Then $$\\label{lin:global-estimate}\n \\|(u,\\lambda)\\|_{X_B}\n \\le C_{D,Y_0,h,\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}}\n \\left\\|\\bigl(L_Bu+\\sum_i\\lambda_i\\chi_{i,B},P_Bu\\bigr)\\right\\|_{Y_B},$$ and this normalized operator is onto. At a true terminal section define $g=u_s(T_B)$ for the prescribed scalar variable in the real outward coordinate. If $t=t(s)$ is a local log coordinate, this means $g=H u_t(T_B)$ with $H=t_s$. For this prescribed exit derivative the right hand side is augmented by $\\rho_B(T_B)^{-1}\\|g\\|_{\\mathcal T^N_{E(T_B),h}}$ at each terminal section; the sum over the fixed finite list of exits is understood. The thresholds and constant may depend on the fixed rate, but are independent of $B$ and of the lengths of the exhausted conical ends. Removing $\\rho_B$, or converting a relative height to physical height on a cap, costs at most a fixed power of $B$. The preliminary construction uses $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}=2.2$; a source with a fixed higher Taylor growth rate is permitted by choosing $\\alpha_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ equal to or larger than that rate.           "anchor": "stmt-lin-shielding",
          "exact_quote": "On a fixed log-length overlap suppose the hypotheses of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a> hold with $E\\asymp B^{-2}$.           "anchor": "stmt-arr-first-variation",
          "exact_quote": "At fixed compact observation values, a differentiable family of the preceding exact normalized solves satisfies $$\\frac{dG}{d\\tau}\n   =\\sum_{\\text{exits}}\\text{boundary position and momentum terms}.$$ This algebraic identity holds for prescribed artificial Neumann data satisfying <a href=\"#arr:allowed-traces\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"arr:allowed-traces\">[arr:allowed-traces]</a>, and for the refined class later proved in [jump:compatibility](#jump:compatibility).           "exact_quote": "For any sufficiently high real-coefficient polynomial path $p_0(s)$ with the specified opening jet and any sufficiently large fixed $\\ell$, the arrays $G_\\pm(s,p_0(s)+s^\\ell h)$, uniformly for $h$ in a fixed complex ball, have the formal stationary expansion of Gevrey order $1/k$.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-arr-formal-replacement",
          "exact_quote": "Let $f_0=\\mathcal F-\\mathcal F(0)$ and $f_i=\\partial_{p_i}\\mathcal F$. There are finitely many expressions $g_1,\\dots,g_r$, each obtained from these formal series and coordinates by finitely many partial differentiations and polynomial operations, such that the following holds. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-fixed-center-tangent**: At each first singular point, the full family of fixed-center rescalings converges to a single smooth multiplicity-one homothetic self-shrinker flow, including its ambient position and axes.
- **invariant-all-endpoint-representative**: Almost-everywhere equality with the smooth homothetic reference determines every interior time slice when the local integrability and all-endpoint Brakke conditions hold.
- **invariant-opening-arc-exclusion**: A real formal critical arc through the origin has identically vanishing cylindrical opening coordinates.
- **invariant-finite-order-obstruction**: A single exponent controls the openings by the gradient and truncation remainder of every sufficiently high fixed action truncation; the neighborhood and comparison constant may depend on the truncation.
- **invariant-localized-gradient**: The Gaussian defect together with the localization tail controls the action gap, opening coordinates, compact graph height, and compact base multipliers. The gradient and opening exponents remain fixed as the localization loss varies.
- **invariant-finite-length-fixed-frame**: Summable rescaled motion closes the graphical bootstrap and yields smooth convergence on every fixed compact set at every rescaled time in the original ambient frame.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-moving-center**: Apply fixed-frame tangent uniqueness to blowups centered along a moving sequence of spatial points. -> The rescaling family would change the center required by the stated convergence result.
- **anti-post-singular-continuation**: Use tangent uniqueness to select a continuation or surgery after a singularity. -> A unique backward tangent does not supply a forward continuation rule or a surgery construction.
- **anti-unqualified-initial-geometry**: Extend the conclusion directly to immersed surfaces, surfaces with boundary, or arbitrary ambient dimensions. -> The geometric tangent and end-structure inputs have only the stated initial-surface and ambient scope.
- **anti-exceptional-slice-redefinition**: Infer equality at every time from spacetime weight equality alone. -> Spacetime equality determines slices only almost everywhere; it does not by itself fix exceptional representatives.
- **anti-opening-series-analyticity**: Treat the formal opening expansion as a convergent analytic surface family. -> Coefficientwise solvability and polynomial growth do not establish convergence in the opening variables.
- **anti-coarse-inverse-on-power-error**: Apply the polynomial physical inverse directly to the original exterior error and assume a nonlinear contraction follows. -> The polynomial inverse can consume the smallness needed for the exterior nonlinear solve.
- **anti-relative-phase-only**: Compare adverse end contributions using only relative agreement of their squared matching heights. -> A relative height error can still change the Gaussian exponential substantially and obscure cancellation.
- **anti-incomplete-graph**: Propagate a selected local sheet while ignoring other surface components inside the same ball. -> The graphical propagation argument requires coverage of the whole surface intersection and exclusion of additional sheets.
- **anti-sampled-numerical-certificate**: Treat agreement among finitely many simulated blowups or truncated coefficient checks as certification of tangent-flow uniqueness. -> Such checks do not decide convergence of the full rescaling family or the analytic and geometric hypotheses on complete ends.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The target result is convergence and uniqueness for a continuum family of smooth surface rescalings, supported by infinite-end estimates, formal series, analytic existence arguments, and bootstrap limits. The source states: "The rescaled flow converges smoothly on every fixed compact set, at all rescaled times, to $S$ in the original ambient coordinates." Its finite-power step is existential: "The exponent $m$ is independent of $N$." These statements do not specify a finite computational input representation, an effective procedure for constructing the tangent section, or a computable convergence modulus. Finite checks of an auxiliary recurrence or phase identity would cover only that auxiliary calculation and would not decide the triptych's continuum invariants.

          "exact_quote": "For <a href=\"#lin:cylinder-operator\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:cylinder-operator\">[lin:cylinder-operator]</a>, and for perturbations satisfying the normalized decay condition below, a weight $e^{\\alpha t}$ with $\\alpha\\notin\\{2-j^2:j\\in\\mathbb Z\\}$ gives separated end estimates. Slow data of rate below $\\alpha$ are prescribed at the entrance; slow data of rate above $\\alpha$ are prescribed at infinity (or at the appropriate finite exit). Finite intervals have logarithmic length at least a fixed $\\ell_*>0$, with constants allowed to depend on $\\ell_*$. Crossing a rate changes the solution space by exactly the corresponding angular modes. Estimates hold with every fixed number of log-coordinate derivatives when the source has the corresponding regularity, with an arbitrarily small loss in a stated polynomial power.*\n\n\n*Here the second-order differential perturbation $Q=\\mathcal L-\\mathcal L_{\\mathrm{cyl}}$ retains the strict principal accretivity of Lemma <a href=\"#lin:strip\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lin:strip\">6</a>, with $E\\asymp e^{-2t}$, and, for the chosen $0<\\eta<1$, has the following gain on every fixed weight used in the assertion: $$\\label{lin:normalized-decay}\n \\|Qv\\|_{Y_{e^{(\\beta-2+\\eta)t},h}}\n       \\le C_{\\beta,h,\\eta}\\|v\\|_{X_{e^{\\beta t},h}}.$$ The analogous bound is required after the fixed translations and commutations used to obtain derivative estimates. Thus the changes of the radial, mixed, and angular principal coefficients are measured in their respective units $E$, $\\sqrt E$, and $1$; lower coefficient terms may instead be measured in the corresponding coefficient–module operator norm. Ordinary absolute decay of the radial coefficient is not the condition in <a href=\"#lin:normalized-decay\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"lin:normalized-decay\">[lin:normalized-decay]</a>.*\n\n\n*Consequently, on each cylindrical end and for every small $\\eta>0$, $$\\label{lin:end-expansion}\n R-\\sqrt2=O(z^{-2+\\eta}),\\qquad\n J=c z^2+z(\\ell\\cdot e_r)+O(z^\\eta)$$ for a Gaussian Jacobi solution with compact source. If $c=0$, subtracting the exact infinitesimal rotation with tilt $\\ell$ leaves $O(z^{-2+\\eta})$. End solutions with arbitrary prescribed $c,\\ell$ exist, and their inward cutoffs have compact Jacobi source.",

          "exact_quote": "Let $\\kappa$ be the number of cylindrical ends.
